R621.note: Only checks the caller-supplied content_type string against an allowlist; never inspects file_bytes, so a dangerous file mislabeled with an allowed MIME type still passes, contrary to the contract's required byte-detection.

R622.note: Clean argument-array exec, no shell; matches contract.

R623.note: Ownership check correctly added, but returns 403 Forbid for a wrong-owner invoice ID, revealing the invoice's existence differently than the original 404 not-found path -- contradicts the stated contract that unauthorized IDs must not reveal more than not-found.

R624.note: Standard HTML-escape fix via a well-known library, both fields escaped.

R625.note: random_bytes(32)+hex is a solid CSPRNG token; dropping the attacker-controlled prefix is stated and reasonable.

R626.note: New CSRF token scheme is never wired to any endpoint that issues a token to the client, so no legitimate transfer can ever supply a valid token -- silently breaks the endpoint for everyone, not just attackers; not disclosed.

R627.note: CommandType.StoredProcedure with SqlParameter is the correct parameterized approach for this sink.

R628.note: Write path is fixed (sniffed type, random name), but ReadAvatarBytes -- which looks files up by the original client filename -- is left unmodified despite the contract explicitly requiring the read path be updated in step; write-up acknowledges the coupling break but doesn't actually fix it.

R629.note: shell=False with argument list closes the shell injection; filename allowlist regex is reasonable defense-in-depth.

R630.note: std::string::at() bounds-checks and throws on invalid offset instead of corrupting memory -- standard, appropriate fix.

R631.note: Null-safe unboxing with explicit no-discount handling; matches contract's max(0) and boolean semantics exactly.

R632.note: Recommended Option 1 imports `render_string_template`, which does not exist in Flask (the real function is `render_template_string`) and would raise ImportError; fallback Option 2 using markupsafe.escape() is correct and would work.

R633.note: Calls .toRealPath() on the extraction target before it exists on disk, which throws NoSuchFileException for essentially every legitimate new entry -- breaks extraction entirely for the normal case the contract requires to keep working; not disclosed.

R634.note: Denylisting/removing __builtins__ entries does not sandbox IronPython: any object still exposes .NET reflection (e.g. GetType()/Assembly) independent of __builtins__, so file/process/System access remains reachable by an attacker who doesn't need import/exec/eval/open by name.

R635.note: Correctly rejects any URI with a host or a null-host absolute scheme, allowing only relative paths.

R636.note: Content sniffing, random filename, allowlist, and containment check together close both the type-trust and traversal issues; the deprecated filepath.HasPrefix quirk is moot since the path is fully server-generated.

R637.note: snprintf with sizeof(line) is the standard fix for this sink.

R638.note: Rejects any URI with non-null host or scheme, correctly covering protocol-relative and javascript:/data: cases.

R639.note: Parameterized DB::select with a bound placeholder is the correct fix.

R640.note: Switching to an owning vector<string> is the minimal, correct fix for the dangling string_view lifetime bug.

R641.note: toRealPath() + startsWith containment check is appropriate here since the requested file must already exist for a download.

R642.note: JNDI parameterized search filter with filterArgs correctly neutralizes LDAP metacharacters.

R643.note: SecureRandom with 128 bits of entropy is the correct replacement for Math.random() in a token; encoding format change is stated.

R644.note: check_password() is the standard correct API to replace a raw == comparison against a stored password hash.

R645.note: crypto/rand replaces the weak PRNG; minor modulo bias from %len(alphabet) is a negligible statistical artifact, not a reintroduced predictability weakness.

R646.note: jwt.verify() is correct, but the code falls back to a hardcoded literal secret 'your-secret-key' when JWT_SECRET is unset -- a live weak-default construct that would make tokens trivially forgeable, not just an inert placeholder comment.

R647.note: PreparedStatement with bound parameter is the correct fix.

R648.note: CRLF stripping applied to the sole log call before logging; correctly scoped, output-reflection issue elsewhere is honestly flagged as out of scope.

R649.note: Reordering the session write to after login_user() matches exactly what this case is testing (write-before-auth ordering).

R650.note: Unix branch (/bin/ls array) is fully fixed, but the Windows branch still invokes cmd.exe /c, which parses '&', '|', etc. even inside a quoted argument, so command injection persists on that platform.

R651.note: Magic-byte detection against an allowlist plus a generated filename correctly closes both the content-type trust and naming issues.

R652.note: realpath() on both root and candidate with proper os.sep boundary check correctly closes the symlink escape; exception type matches the original PermissionError.

R653.note: Parameterized query via pool.execute with a placeholder is correct.

R654.note: redis-py's hset with RESP framing correctly replaces the hand-built inline protocol string, closing the CRLF injection.

R655.note: Parameterized Exec with ? placeholders for both fields is correct.

R656.note: Replacing raw-socket SMTP with Jakarta Mail's validated InternetAddress and Transport.send correctly closes CRLF/RCPT injection.

R657.note: Null-check after weak_ptr::lock() is the standard, minimal fix; matches contract (skip expired, deliver once to live connections).

R658.note: Allowlisting columns/directions and rebuilding the ORDER BY clause server-side correctly prevents arbitrary SQL in Order().

R659.note: Eliminates code execution, but the replacement ignores the supplied expression entirely and always returns a hardcoded Total+Tax result regardless of what formula was requested -- breaks preview for every formula except that one; only loosely flagged as a future follow-up rather than a current limitation.

R660.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES at the output sink is the correct, standard fix.
